text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore government launches National Programme on Best Practices to help companies become world-class businesses.
- Singapore and Australia end Joint Ministerial Committee meeting with new initiatives for further bilateral cooperation.
- Australian Prime Minister John Howard indicates possibility of visit to Singapore in first half of next year.
- Applications to withdraw cash from Central Provident Fund for private property purchases fall more than 50 percent.
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says fall of ringgit is not linked to threats of sanctions by United states against state oil firm Petronas.
- Short sellers of Labroy Marine shares feel the pinch of buying-in exercise by Stock Exchange of Singapore, with 2.3 million shares bought at Singapore $1.20 each.
- Japanese telecommunications giant Nippon Telephone & Telegraph is considering moving its multimedia research and development activities to Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor.
- Malaysian ringgit hits six-month low of Malaysian $2.5330 against the U.S. dollar and then recovers at end of day to $2.5234.
- Citibank will provide margin financing for most Malaysian shares, loan stock, bonds and warrants.
- Mohammad 'Bob' Hasan and Putera Sampoerna disclose that they together control up to 25 percent of vehicle maker PT Astra International.
- Singatronics Ltd announces the closure of its Singapore plant and its U.S.-based programme management arm.
